land.text: 'The southern islands of New South Wales' (Van Diemen's Land)

predecessors.note: British settlement began in 1803 under New South Wales; 'it became a separate colony in 1825' (Van Diemen's Land page).

land.text: Tasmania with Macquarie Island, which became a state of the Commonwealth on 1 January 1901

successors.note: The State of Tasmania is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier from 1 January 1901.

capitals.name: Hobart Town (Hobart)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Hobart'; the text names 'Hobart Town'.

correction.text: 'The southern islands of New South Wales were made the Colony of Van Diemen's Land': the island of Tasmania (Norfolk Island, also held 26 September 1844 to 1 November 1856, has no grid cell)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern Tasmania, about 0.06 M km2 by the gazetteer. Neither the Van Diemen's Land page nor the Territorial evolution page gives an infobox area. Norfolk Island and the Bass Strait islands add no cells.

correction.text: 'Macquarie Island became part of Tasmania' (17 June 1880)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Tasmania with Macquarie Island (one cell) from 17 June 1880 to federation.

region.text: Van Diemen's Land, 'the southern islands of New South Wales' (Territorial evolution of Australia)

ledger.note: 1825: Van Diemen's Land becomes a separate colony. 'On 3 December 1825, he proclaimed the establishment of the independent colony, of which he became governor for three days.' British settlement had begun in 1803 under New South Wales ('a settlement in 1803 before it became a separate colony in 1825').

region.text: Norfolk Island was transferred from New South Wales to Van Diemen's Land

ledger.note: 1844: Norfolk Island is transferred from New South Wales to Van Diemen's Land (26 September 1844). No grid cell.
1856: Van Diemen's Land becomes Tasmania. 'the name of the island and colony was officially changed to Tasmania on 1 January 1856.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Norfolk Island became its own colony, split from Tasmania

ledger.note: 1856: Norfolk Island becomes its own colony, split from Tasmania (1 November 1856). No grid cell.

region.text: Macquarie Island became part of Tasmania

ledger.note: 1880: Macquarie Island becomes part of Tasmania (17 June 1880). One grid cell.

region.text: Tasmania with Macquarie Island as it stood in 1900

ledger.note: 1901: Tasmania federates (1 January 1901): 'On 1 January 1901, these colonies, excepting New Zealand (who chose not to join), became states' of the Commonwealth. The State of Tasmania is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier.

wars.name: Black Line (offensive of the Black War)
wars.outcome: 'In 1830 Lieutenant-Governor Arthur attempted to end the "Black War" through a massive offensive'; the frontier war in Van Diemen's Land followed settlement from the mid-1820s. No border moved; the Aboriginal Tasmanians were stateless.
wars.note: The Australian frontier wars page gives the Black Line (1830) but not the Black War's start and end years; the Van Diemen's Land page mentions the Black War only in a film description. from and to are therefore the year of the Black Line, not the war's span.

certainty.note: An island colony: the border is the coast. Norfolk Island (1844 to 1856) and Macquarie Island (from 1880) are single points and add no land border.

sources.title: Territorial evolution of Australia
sources.note: Boundary changes: Norfolk Island (1844, 1856), Macquarie Island (1880), federation (1901).

sources.title: Van Diemen's Land
sources.note: Settlement 1803, separate colony 3 December 1825, renamed Tasmania 1 January 1856, capital Hobart, 1853 end of transportation.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 3 pages used: Van Diemen's Land, Territorial evolution of Australia, Australian frontier wars.
Not on the pages opened: the Hobart (Sullivans Cove, 1804) and Launceston (1806) foundations, the Black War span, the 1853 end of transportation is only 'the 1853 abolition of penal transportation'. The Van Diemen's Land page gives self-government as 'granted ... in 1856' and 'self-governing in 1855' (disagreeing); not a border event. The colony of Norfolk Island (1856 to 1914 on the Territorial evolution page: 'Norfolk Island became its own colony' on 1 November 1856 and 'became the Territory of Norfolk Island' on 1 July 1914) has a dossier, colony-of-norfolk-island, written later in this run by oc-02-x (no grid cell). The Tasmanian shape ignores the Furneaux group and Bass Strait islands (below the grid).
